GENERATE_SERIES.summary: Build an array of evenly spaced integers.

overloads.label: GENERATE_SERIES(stop)
overloads.documentation: Builds the series as an ARRAY in a single row. `GENERATE_SERIES(10)` starts at 1; `GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10)` and `GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10, 2)` start where they say. `stop` is included when it falls on a step boundary. A step pointing away from `stop` yields an EMPTY array; a step of zero is refused. Arguments must be integer CONSTANTS. To get one ROW per value instead - which is what gap-filling and joining against a dense axis need - use the table spelling, `FROM GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10) AS g`, which also accepts floats and, with an INTERVAL step, timestamps.

parameters.label: stop
parameters.documentation: Last value of the series, included when it falls on a step boundary. Must be a constant expression.

A step pointing away from `stop` yields an EMPTY array; a step of zero is refused. Arguments must be integer CONSTANTS. To get one ROW per value instead - which is what gap-filling and joining against a dense axis need - use the table spelling, `FROM GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10) AS g`, which also accepts floats and, with an INTERVAL step, timestamps.

parameters.label: start
parameters.documentation: First value of the series. Must be a constant expression.

parameters.label: stop
parameters.documentation: Last value of the series, included when it falls on a step boundary. Must be a constant expression.

overloads.label: GENERATE_SERIES(start, stop, step)
overloads.documentation: Builds the series as an ARRAY in a single row. `GENERATE_SERIES(10)` starts at 1; `GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10)` and `GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10, 2)` start where they say. `stop` is included when it falls on a step boundary. A step pointing away from `stop` yields an EMPTY array; a step of zero is refused. Arguments must be integer CONSTANTS. To get one ROW per value instead - which is what gap-filling and joining against a dense axis need - use the table spelling, `FROM GENERATE_SERIES(1, 10) AS g`, which also accepts floats and, with an INTERVAL step, timestamps.

parameters.label: start
parameters.documentation: First value of the series. Must be a constant expression.

parameters.label: stop
parameters.documentation: Last value of the series, included when it falls on a step boundary. Must be a constant expression.

Matching is only as semantic as the active EMBED capability: the built-in embedder is a lexical hashed projection, so by default MATCH behaves as a case-insensitive exact match rather than a meaning-based one. Install a semantic embedding capability, and/or tune `match_threshold`, to change that. Empty or stopword-only text embeds to a zero vector, giving an undefined (NaN) similarity, which never matches.
overloads.notes: Canonical form is `MATCH(str) AGAINST(pattern)`. Opteryx normalizes this syntax to an internal helper.

parameters.documentation: The SET of characters to strip, not a substring to match: `TRIM(BOTH 'ab' FROM 'baXab')` is `X`. Must be constant. Omitted, ASCII whitespace is stripped. Omit it (`TRIM(str)`) to strip ASCII whitespace; the direction-only spelling `TRIM(BOTH FROM str)` is not accepted.

overloads.label: TRUNC(num, [scale...])
overloads.documentation: Truncates a numeric value toward zero at the requested scale.

parameters.label: scale
parameters.documentation: Decimal scale to keep before truncating toward zero. Optional. Can be repeated.

overloads.notes: Truncation is performed toward zero rather than toward negative infinity.

overloads.label: TRUNC(value, unit)
overloads.documentation: Truncates a temporal value to the start of the specified unit.

parameters.label: value
parameters.documentation: Date, time, or timestamp value to truncate.

parameters.label: unit
parameters.documentation: Granularity to truncate to, such as `day`, `month`, or `year`. Must be a constant expression.

overloads.notes: Truncates to the start of the specified unit. The `unit` argument must be a constant expression. This overload is reachable only for a DATE LITERAL, which is constant-folded at plan time: over a DATE COLUMN there is no native kernel and the call is refused with "outside the c-native kernel set". Cast the column to TIMESTAMP to truncate it. Also spelled `DATE_TRUNC(unit, value)` - unit FIRST.
